problems.title: Distinct steering configurations append to an indistinguishable output file
problems.source_location: Official RICE intervention.py, run, lines 35–43, 50–54 and 106–114
claim: For nonempty selected-expert settings, the evaluation function overwrites its configuration-specific filename component with normal, although it still passes the actual steering multiplier and expert set to the model.
analysis: Fix dataset, sampling arguments and output directory, and choose expert string 29:126;39:182 with \(\beta=4\) and then \(\beta=64\). Both valid settings enter the same nonempty branch, assign the identical filename component normal, and open that path in append mode. Each record stores only data identifier, problem and response, so the two interventions cannot be distinguished from those records. Separate output directories or external manifests can avoid the pooling; a single isolated invocation does not mix settings.
result: The official release loses intervention provenance when those settings share an output directory. The source trace establishes the collision without model execution; it does not establish that any published accuracy was computed from mixed outputs.
repair: Keep the steering/expert component for nonempty configurations and use normal only for the baseline; store intervention metadata with each output. The proposed filename change addresses this collision but not complete run identity.
